fr: Nous réservons une table pour huit heures.
en: We are reserving a table for eight o'clock.
ipa: /nu ʁe.zɛʁ.vɔ̃z‿yn ta.blə puʁ ɥi.tœʁ/
notes: The liaison between 'huit' and 'heures' produces a /t/ sound that is easy to miss when writing from dictation.

fr: Vous avez une table pour deux ce soir.
en: You have a table for two this evening.
ipa: /vu.z‿a.ve yn ta.blə puʁ dø sə swaʁ/
notes: 'Vous avez' liaises so the final s of vous is pronounced as /z/ before the vowel.

fr: Les enfants adorent les crêpes au chocolat.
en: The children love chocolate crepes.
ipa: /le.z‿ɑ̃.fɑ̃ a.dɔʁ le kʁɛp o ʃɔ.kɔ.la/
notes: 'Les enfants' requires the liaison z, easy to miss when writing quickly from dictation.

fr: Ils ont très faim avant le repas.
en: They are very hungry before the meal.
ipa: /il.z‿ɔ̃ tʁɛ fɛ̃ a.vɑ̃ lə ʁə.pa/
notes: The liaison in 'ils ont' can be confused with 'ils sont', so listen for the nasal vowel that follows.

fr: Cet homme commande un plat du jour.
en: This man orders the dish of the day.
ipa: /sɛ.t‿ɔm kɔ.mɑ̃d œ̃ pla dy ʒuʁ/
notes: The liaison after 'cet' produces a /t/ sound even though the masculine form looks silent.

fr: Nous avons deux assiettes de soupe chaude.
en: We have two plates of hot soup.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ dø.z‿a.sjɛt də sup ʃod/
notes: Two liaisons in a row, nous avons and deux assiettes, can trick the ear into hearing extra words.

fr: Un grand appétit accompagne ce repas copieux.
en: A big appetite goes with this hearty meal.
ipa: /œ̃ ɡʁɑ̃.t‿a.pe.ti a.kɔ̃.pa.ɲ sə ʁə.pa kɔ.pjø/
notes: 'Grand appétit' liaises with a /t/ sound even though grand ends in a silent d.

fr: Le restaurant ouvre à midi.
en: The restaurant opens at noon.
ipa: /lə ʁɛs.tɔ.ʁɑ̃ u.vʁ a mi.di/
notes: The final t of 'restaurant' is always silent, a common spelling slip in dictée.

fr: Le plat du jour est délicieux.
en: The dish of the day is delicious.
ipa: /lə pla dy ʒuʁ ɛ de.li.sjø/
notes: Both the t in 'plat' and the final consonant sound of 'est' stay silent.

fr: Le pain chaud sent très bon.
en: The warm bread smells very good.
ipa: /lə pɛ̃ ʃo sɑ̃ tʁɛ bɔ̃/
notes: The d at the end of 'chaud' is never pronounced, though it must still be written.

fr: Le client attend son dessert.
en: The customer is waiting for dessert.
ipa: /lə kli.jɑ̃ a.tɑ̃ sɔ̃ de.sɛʁ/
notes: The final t of 'client' is silent, just like the d ending of 'attend' in speech.

fr: Il choisit un dessert au chocolat.
en: He chooses a chocolate dessert.
ipa: /il ʃwa.zi œ̃ de.sɛʁ o ʃɔ.kɔ.la/
notes: The final t of 'choisit' is silent, so learners often forget to write it.

fr: Le riz accompagne le poisson grillé.
en: The rice comes with the grilled fish.
ipa: /lə ʁi a.kɔ̃.pa.ɲ lə pwa.sɔ̃ ɡʁi.je/
notes: The z at the end of 'riz' is completely silent in speech.

fr: Le serveur apporte beaucoup de pain.
en: The waiter brings a lot of bread.
ipa: /lə sɛʁ.vœʁ a.pɔʁt bo.ku də pɛ̃/
notes: The final p of 'beaucoup' is silent, a classic spelling trap in dictée.

fr: Le vin blanc accompagne bien le poisson.
en: White wine pairs well with fish.
ipa: /lə vɛ̃ blɑ̃ a.kɔ̃.pa.ɲ bjɛ̃ lə pwa.sɔ̃/
notes: Three different nasal vowels appear close together, in vin, blanc and bien, and are easy to mix up.

fr: J'ai très faim avant le dîner.
en: I am very hungry before dinner.
ipa: /ʒe tʁɛ fɛ̃ a.vɑ̃ lə di.ne/
notes: The nasal vowel in 'faim' is easy to confuse with other nasal spellings like fin.

fr: Le client demande du pain blanc.
en: The customer asks for white bread.
ipa: /lə kli.jɑ̃ də.mɑ̃d dy pɛ̃ blɑ̃/
notes: Two nasal vowels, an and in, sit side by side and must be spelled differently despite similar sounds.

fr: Le restaurant sert un excellent gratin.
en: The restaurant serves an excellent gratin.
ipa: /lə ʁɛs.tɔ.ʁɑ̃ sɛʁ œ̃.n‿ɛk.sɛ.lɑ̃ ɡʁa.tɛ̃/
notes: The nasal endings in and an both appear here and are easy to swap when writing quickly.

fr: Le menu propose un poulet aux champignons.
en: The menu offers chicken with mushrooms.
ipa: /lə mə.ny pʁɔ.poz œ̃ pu.lɛ o ʃɑ̃.pi.ɲɔ̃/
notes: The nasal vowel in 'champignons' combines with a silent final s, a double trap for spelling.

fr: Elle prend un dessert avec des amandes.
en: She has a dessert with almonds.
ipa: /ɛl pʁɑ̃ œ̃ de.sɛʁ a.vɛk de.z‿a.mɑ̃d/
notes: The nasal vowel in 'prend' sounds identical to 'prends', so context decides the correct ending.

fr: Le pain complet sent bon le matin.
en: Whole grain bread smells good in the morning.
ipa: /lə pɛ̃ kɔ̃.plɛ sɑ̃ bɔ̃ lə ma.tɛ̃/
notes: Four nasal vowels appear in this short sentence, each spelled with a different letter combination.

fr: Le serveur a la carte des desserts.
en: The waiter has the dessert menu.
ipa: /lə sɛʁ.vœʁ a la kaʁt de de.sɛʁ/
notes: The verb form 'a' sounds exactly like the preposition 'à', so only meaning tells them apart.

fr: Où est la table près de la fenêtre ?
en: Where is the table near the window?
ipa: /u ɛ la ta.blə pʁɛ də la fə.nɛtʁ/
notes: 'Où' with an accent means where, while 'ou' without one means or, and they sound identical.

fr: Ces plats sont vraiment délicieux ce soir.
en: These dishes are really delicious tonight.
ipa: /se pla sɔ̃ vʁɛ.mɑ̃ de.li.sjø sə swaʁ/
notes: 'Ces' the demonstrative and 'ses' the possessive sound the same but change the meaning of the sentence.

fr: Le repas est prêt dans la cuisine.
en: The meal is ready in the kitchen.
ipa: /lə ʁə.pa ɛ pʁɛ dɑ̃ la kɥi.zin/
notes: 'Est' the verb and 'et' the conjunction are perfect homophones that only context can separate.

fr: Son verre de vin est déjà vide.
en: His glass of wine is already empty.
ipa: /sɔ̃ vɛʁ də vɛ̃ ɛ de.ʒa vid/
notes: 'Son' meaning his or her sounds exactly like 'sont', the verb form, a frequent dictée mix-up.

fr: La serveuse pose le plat sur la table.
en: The waitress puts the dish on the table.
ipa: /la sɛʁ.vøz poz lə pla syʁ la ta.blə/
notes: 'Sur' meaning on can be confused with 'sûr' meaning certain, distinguished only by the circumflex accent.

fr: J'aime beaucoup ce petit restaurant italien.
en: I really like this little Italian restaurant.
ipa: /ʒɛm bo.ku sə pə.ti ʁɛs.tɔ.ʁɑ̃ i.ta.ljɛ̃/
notes: 'Je' drops its e before a vowel to become j'aime, a mandatory elision in writing.

fr: L'addition arrive à la fin du repas.
en: The bill arrives at the end of the meal.
ipa: /la.di.sjɔ̃ a.ʁiv a la fɛ̃ dy ʁə.pa/
notes: 'La addition' is never written that way, the article must elide to l'addition before the vowel.

fr: Qu'il choisisse vite, le serveur attend.
en: Let him choose quickly, the waiter is waiting.
ipa: /kil ʃwa.zis vit lə sɛʁ.vœʁ a.tɑ̃/
notes: 'Que il' always contracts to qu'il in writing, never left as two separate words.

fr: J'adore le fromage à la fin du repas.
en: I love cheese at the end of the meal.
ipa: /ʒa.dɔʁ lə fʁɔ.maʒ a la fɛ̃ dy ʁə.pa/
notes: The subject je elides before the vowel of adore, forming the single written word j'adore.

fr: D'habitude, elle commande une soupe à l'oignon.
en: Usually, she orders French onion soup.
ipa: /da.bi.tyd ɛl kɔ.mɑ̃d yn sup a lɔ.ɲɔ̃/
notes: 'De habitude' is impossible in French, the preposition must elide to d'habitude.

fr: L'eau gazeuse coûte un euro de plus.
en: Sparkling water costs one euro more.
ipa: /lo ɡa.zøz kut œ̃.n‿ø.ʁo də plys/
notes: 'Le eau' cannot exist, the article elides to l'eau before the vowel sound.

fr: Les tables sont toutes réservées ce soir.
en: The tables are all reserved tonight.
ipa: /le ta.blə sɔ̃ tut ʁe.zɛʁ.ve sə swaʁ/
notes: The plural agreement adds a silent s to both toutes and réservées, unheard but required in writing.

fr: Les entrées sont fraîches et bien présentées.
en: The starters are fresh and nicely presented.
ipa: /le.z‿ɑ̃.tʁe sɔ̃ fʁɛʃ e bjɛ̃ pʁe.zɑ̃.te/
notes: 'Fraîches' takes a silent feminine plural ending that matches entrées but is not heard aloud.

fr: Ces assiettes sont très chaudes, attention.
en: These plates are very hot, be careful.
ipa: /se.z‿a.sjɛt sɔ̃ tʁɛ ʃod a.tɑ̃.sjɔ̃/
notes: 'Chaudes' agrees in the feminine plural with assiettes, adding a silent e and s.

fr: Les boissons fraîches sont servies immédiatement.
en: Cold drinks are served immediately.
ipa: /le bwa.sɔ̃ fʁɛʃ sɔ̃ sɛʁ.vi i.me.dja.tmɑ̃/
notes: 'Servies' carries a silent feminine plural ending that agrees with boissons.

fr: Mes plats préférés sont toujours italiens.
en: My favorite dishes are always Italian.
ipa: /me pla pʁe.fe.ʁe sɔ̃ tu.ʒuʁ i.ta.ljɛ̃/
notes: 'Préférés' and 'italiens' both add a silent plural s that has to be written even though unheard.

fr: Les glaces maison sont vraiment délicieuses.
en: The homemade ice creams are really delicious.
ipa: /le ɡlas mɛ.zɔ̃ sɔ̃ vʁɛ.mɑ̃ de.li.sjøz/
notes: 'Délicieuses' agrees in the feminine plural, adding letters that stay silent in pronunciation.

fr: La serveuse pose une petite carafe d'eau.
en: The waitress puts down a small carafe of water.
ipa: /la sɛʁ.vøz poz yn pə.tit ka.ʁaf do/
notes: The mute e in 'petite' is barely heard but must still be written before the final consonant.

fr: Cette table est libre pour le déjeuner.
en: This table is free for lunch.
ipa: /sɛt ta.blə ɛ li.bʁə puʁ lə de.ʒœ.ne/
notes: The final mute e of 'table' is silent but keeps the preceding consonant sound in place.

fr: Une petite salade suffit pour commencer.
en: A small salad is enough to start.
ipa: /yn pə.tit sa.lad sy.fi puʁ kɔ.mɑ̃.se/
notes: The mute e inside 'petite' can disappear in fast speech, tempting learners to drop it in writing too.

fr: Le serveur apporte une carafe d'eau fraîche.
en: The waiter brings a carafe of cold water.
ipa: /lə sɛʁ.vœʁ a.pɔʁt yn ka.ʁaf do fʁɛʃ/
notes: The final mute e of 'carafe' is never pronounced but always written.

fr: Cette assiette semble un peu trop pleine.
en: This plate seems a bit too full.
ipa: /sɛt a.sjɛt sɑ̃bl œ̃ pø tʁo plɛn/
notes: The mute e at the end of 'semble' disappears in speech yet stays essential in spelling.

fr: Notre table donne sur la petite terrasse.
en: Our table looks out on the small terrace.
ipa: /nɔtʁ ta.blə dɔn syʁ la pə.tit tɛ.ʁas/
notes: Several mute e endings in this sentence are silent in speech but obligatory in writing.

fr: Nous mangeons une glace après le repas.
en: We eat ice cream after the meal.
ipa: /nu mɑ̃.ʒɔ̃ yn ɡlas a.pʁɛ lə ʁə.pa/
notes: The extra e in 'mangeons' keeps the g soft, an easy letter to forget when writing quickly.

fr: Le serveur commence son service à midi.
en: The waiter starts his shift at noon.
ipa: /lə sɛʁ.vœʁ kɔ.mɑ̃s sɔ̃ sɛʁ.vis a mi.di/
notes: The c in 'commence' needs no cedilla here since e follows, unlike forms such as commençons.

fr: Le glaçon fond vite dans le verre.
en: The ice cube melts quickly in the glass.
ipa: /lə ɡla.sɔ̃ fɔ̃ vit dɑ̃ lə vɛʁ/
notes: The cedilla under the c in 'glaçon' is required before a and o to keep the soft s sound.

fr: Le cuisinier prépare un plat épicé.
en: The cook prepares a spicy dish.
ipa: /lə kɥi.zi.nje pʁe.paʁ œ̃ pla e.pi.se/
notes: 'Épicé' needs two different accents, an acute at the start and another before the final syllable.

fr: Ce restaurant reçoit beaucoup de clients.
en: This restaurant receives a lot of customers.
ipa: /sə ʁɛs.tɔ.ʁɑ̃ ʁə.swa bo.ku də kli.jɑ̃/
notes: The cedilla in 'reçoit' is essential before o to keep the s sound instead of a k sound.

fr: Le serveur répète la commande deux fois.
en: The waiter repeats the order twice.
ipa: /lə sɛʁ.vœʁ ʁe.pɛt la kɔ.mɑ̃d dø fwa/
notes: 'Répète' carries two different accents, acute then grave, that change the vowel sound in each syllable.

fr: Elle est allée au restaurant hier soir.
en: She went to the restaurant last night.
ipa: /ɛl ɛ.t‿a.le o ʁɛs.tɔ.ʁɑ̃ jɛʁ swaʁ/
notes: With être, the past participle 'allée' agrees with the feminine subject, adding a silent e.

fr: Nous sommes arrivés en retard au dîner.
en: We arrived late for dinner.
ipa: /nu sɔm a.ʁi.ve ɑ̃ ʁə.taʁ o di.ne/
notes: 'Arrivés' agrees with the plural subject nous, adding a silent s that is never heard.

fr: La salade qu'il a commandée était excellente.
en: The salad he ordered was excellent.
ipa: /la sa.lad kil a kɔ.mɑ̃.de e.tɛ ɛk.sɛ.lɑ̃t/
notes: The past participle agrees with 'salade' placed before the verb, adding a silent feminine e.

fr: Les plats qu'elle a choisis étaient copieux.
en: The dishes she chose were generous.
ipa: /le pla kɛl a ʃwa.zi e.tɛ kɔ.pjø/
notes: 'Choisis' agrees with the preceding plural object plats, an ending that stays silent in speech.

fr: Ils sont partis avant la fin du repas.
en: They left before the end of the meal.
ipa: /il sɔ̃ paʁ.ti a.vɑ̃ la fɛ̃ dy ʁə.pa/
notes: With être, 'partis' agrees with the plural masculine subject ils, adding a silent s.

fr: Les tables ont été nettoyées avant l'ouverture.
en: The tables were cleaned before opening.
ipa: /le ta.blə ɔ̃ e.te nɛ.twa.je a.vɑ̃ lu.vɛʁ.tyʁ/
notes: 'Nettoyées' agrees with the feminine plural subject tables, an ending that is silent when spoken.

fr: Elle a réservé une table à huit heures.
en: She booked a table for eight o'clock.
ipa: /ɛl a ʁe.zɛʁ.ve yn ta.blə a ɥi.tœʁ/
notes: The verb 'a' and the preposition 'à' sound identical but only one takes an accent.

fr: On a commandé deux desserts au chocolat.
en: We ordered two chocolate desserts.
ipa: /ɔ̃ a kɔ.mɑ̃.de dø de.sɛʁ o ʃɔ.kɔ.la/
notes: 'On' the pronoun and 'ont' the verb form sound the same, only context reveals which is meant.

fr: Ils ont mangé où le serveur leur a proposé.
en: They ate where the waiter suggested to them.
ipa: /il.z‿ɔ̃ mɑ̃.ʒe u lə sɛʁ.vœʁ lœʁ a pʁɔ.po.ze/
notes: 'Où' with an accent means where, unlike 'ou' meaning or, though they sound identical.

fr: Le client a demandé si le pain était inclus.
en: The customer asked if the bread was included.
ipa: /lə kli.jɑ̃ a də.mɑ̃.de si lə pɛ̃ e.tɛ ɛ̃.kly/
notes: 'Était' and other imperfect forms share the same sound as similar endings, easy to confuse when writing quickly.

fr: Ses amis vont bientôt arriver pour dîner.
en: Her friends are going to arrive soon for dinner.
ipa: /se.z‿a.mi vɔ̃ bjɛ̃.to a.ʁi.ve puʁ di.ne/
notes: 'Ses' the possessive sounds exactly like 'ces' and 'c'est', distinguished only by spelling and meaning.

fr: Le repas était prêt et le vin aussi.
en: The meal was ready and the wine too.
ipa: /lə ʁə.pa e.tɛ pʁɛ e lə vɛ̃ o.si/
notes: 'Et' the conjunction sounds identical to the verb form 'est', a frequent dictée confusion.

fr: Nous allons commander le menu du jour.
en: We are going to order the set menu.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.lɔ̃ kɔ.mɑ̃.de lə mə.ny dy ʒuʁ/
notes: The infinitive 'commander' ends in the same sound as its past participle commandé, only spelling shows the difference.

fr: Le serveur va apporter l'addition bientôt.
en: The waiter is going to bring the bill soon.
ipa: /lə sɛʁ.vœʁ va a.pɔʁ.te la.di.sjɔ̃ bjɛ̃.to/
notes: 'Apporter' sounds exactly like 'apportez' and 'apporté', so the ending must be chosen from context.

fr: Vous allez adorer ce dessert au caramel.
en: You are going to love this caramel dessert.
ipa: /vu.z‿a.le a.dɔ.ʁe sə de.sɛʁ o ka.ʁa.mɛl/
notes: 'Adorer' and 'adoré' share the same final sound, only the grammatical role decides the correct spelling.

fr: J'ai réservé et j'ai payé un acompte.
en: I booked and I paid a deposit.
ipa: /ʒe ʁe.zɛʁ.ve e ʒe pe.je œ̃.n‿a.kɔ̃t/
notes: 'Réservé' and 'payé' both end in the same closed e sound as their infinitive forms, a constant spelling trap.

fr: Le chef va préparer un plat spécial ce soir.
en: The chef is going to prepare a special dish tonight.
ipa: /lə ʃɛf va pʁe.pa.ʁe œ̃ pla spe.sjal sə swaʁ/
notes: 'Préparer' sounds identical to préparé and préparez, so only the sentence structure tells them apart.

fr: Nous avons goûté un excellent vin rouge.
en: We tasted an excellent red wine.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ ɡu.te œ̃.n‿ɛk.sɛ.lɑ̃ vɛ̃ ʁuʒ/
notes: The liaison in 'nous avons' and again before 'excellent' can hide the true word boundaries.

fr: Ils ont attendu longtemps avant d'être servis.
en: They waited a long time before being served.
ipa: /il.z‿ɔ̃ a.tɑ̃.dy lɔ̃.tɑ̃ a.vɑ̃ dɛtʁ sɛʁ.vi/
notes: The liaison after 'ont' links directly into 'attendu', making the word break hard to hear.

fr: Nous allons essayer les huîtres ce soir.
en: We are going to try the oysters tonight.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.lɔ̃.z‿e.se.je le.z‿ɥitʁ sə swaʁ/
notes: Multiple liaisons chain together here, making it easy to lose track of where each word starts.

fr: Vous avez oublié une fourchette sur la table.
en: You forgot a fork on the table.
ipa: /vu.z‿a.ve u.bli.je yn fuʁ.ʃɛt syʁ la ta.blə/
notes: The liaison in 'vous avez' can be mistaken for the start of the next word if written carelessly.

fr: Le client a pris un dessert au chocolat blanc.
en: The customer had a white chocolate dessert.
ipa: /lə kli.jɑ̃ a pʁi œ̃ de.sɛʁ o ʃɔ.kɔ.la blɑ̃/
notes: Three nasal vowels appear close together and must each be spelled with their own letter combination.

fr: Nous avons pris un menu végétarien ce midi.
en: We had a vegetarian menu at lunch.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ pʁi œ̃ mə.ny ve.ʒe.ta.ʁjɛ̃ sə mi.di/
notes: The nasal ending of 'végétarien' is easy to misspell since it sounds like several other nasal endings.

fr: Elle a pris du vin blanc en entrée.
en: She had white wine with the starter.
ipa: /ɛl a pʁi dy vɛ̃ blɑ̃ ɑ̃.n‿ɑ̃.tʁe/
notes: Three nasal vowels in a row make this sentence a real listening challenge for spelling.

fr: Ils vont commander un gratin dauphinois demain.
en: They are going to order a gratin dauphinois tomorrow.
ipa: /il vɔ̃ kɔ.mɑ̃.de œ̃ ɡʁa.tɛ̃ do.fi.nwa də.mɛ̃/
notes: The nasal vowels in gratin and demain look different in spelling despite sounding alike.

fr: Le dessert est arrivé un peu trop tard.
en: The dessert arrived a bit too late.
ipa: /lə de.sɛʁ ɛ.t‿a.ʁi.ve œ̃ pø tʁo taʁ/
notes: The final d of 'tard' is silent, a common ending learners forget to write.

fr: Le client a beaucoup apprécié le repas.
en: The customer really appreciated the meal.
ipa: /lə kli.jɑ̃ a bo.ku a.pʁe.sje lə ʁə.pa/
notes: The final p of 'beaucoup' stays silent even though it must appear in the spelling.

fr: Nous avons fini notre repas assez tard.
en: We finished our meal quite late.
ipa: /nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ fi.ni nɔtʁ ʁə.pa a.se taʁ/
notes: Both 'assez' and 'tard' end in consonants that are never pronounced but still required in writing.

fr: Le client a trouvé le plat un peu froid.
en: The customer found the dish a little cold.
ipa: /lə kli.jɑ̃ a tʁu.ve lə pla œ̃ pø fʁwa/
notes: The final d in 'froid' is silent, so the word can sound like it simply ends in froi.

fr: Nous n'avons pas encore reçu l'addition.
en: We have not yet received the bill.
ipa: /nu na.vɔ̃ pa.z‿ɑ̃.kɔʁ ʁə.sy la.di.sjɔ̃/
notes: The negation ne elides to n'avons before the vowel, a mandatory contraction in writing.

fr: Elle n'a pas aimé le plat principal.
en: She did not like the main dish.
ipa: /ɛl na pa.z‿ɛ.me lə pla pʁɛ̃.si.pal/
notes: 'Ne a' always contracts to n'a in front of a vowel, never left as two separate words.

fr: L'entrée était plus copieuse que d'habitude.
en: The starter was more generous than usual.
ipa: /lɑ̃.tʁe e.tɛ ply kɔ.pjøz kə da.bi.tyd/
notes: 'La entrée' is impossible in French, the article must elide to l'entrée before the vowel.

fr: Cette petite table était déjà réservée.
en: This small table was already reserved.
ipa: /sɛt pə.tit ta.blə e.tɛ de.ʒa ʁe.zɛʁ.ve/
notes: The mute e endings in petite and table stay silent in speech but are essential in spelling.

fr: Notre table était petite mais très agréable.
en: Our table was small but very pleasant.
ipa: /nɔtʁ ta.blə e.tɛ pə.tit mɛ tʁɛ a.ɡʁe.abl/
notes: The mute e endings in table and petite are silent in speech yet required when writing.
